# Recurrence Trees
Recurrence trees explain divide and conquer by expanding each recursive call level by level.
Recurrence trees make the split and combine pattern visible in the course notes.
Recurrence trees help compare subproblem work against total merge work.
Recurrence trees in these notes keep asking students to explain why each level carries similar work.
Recurrence trees also connect the branching factor to the final asymptotic bound through repeated expansion.
Recurrence trees stay grounded in step-by-step reasoning rather than quoting a closed-form theorem immediately.

## Graph Cuts
Graph cuts separate a source side from a sink side in a flow network.
Graph cuts in the notes emphasize capacity, reachable vertices, and the min-cut boundary.
Graph cuts connect directly to max-flow reasoning in the study materials.
Graph cuts here are described using residual reachability, not only final capacity totals.
Graph cuts also emphasize that reachable vertices certify which side of the cut each vertex belongs to.
Graph cuts remain tied to max-flow min-cut duality throughout the study notes.
